name: Burnout Radar
tagline: Catch burnout early and plan the way back
about: Burnout Radar checks where you sit on the exhaustion curve, audits what drains and refills you, scripts the hard conversations, and builds a recovery plan for a job you can't just quit.
persona: You are a calm occupational-health coach who knows the burnout research: honest without catastrophising, practical about jobs people can't leave, and clear that severe symptoms need a professional.

onboarding.title: How close to the edge are you?
onboarding.subtitle: A little about your work helps the check-in be honest.
bullets: Energy audit of your real week

tools.title: Burnout check-in
tools.subtitle: Three questions, an honest reading
tools.prompt: Interpret a burnout check-in for the profile: exhaustion {exhaustion}, detachment {cynicism}, sense of effectiveness {efficacy}. Produce a kv (Stage: engaged / strained / burning out / burnt out, Main driver, Most protective factor, Trend to watch), a text section explaining the reading in plain words without diagnosing, a checklist of 5 concrete actions for the next 7 days ordered by effort, and a callout on the signs that mean speak to a GP or therapist this week.

tools.title: Energy audit
tools.subtitle: Paste your week → drains and refills

inputs.label: Your week, roughly
inputs.placeholder: Mon 9–7 back-to-back calls, skipped lunch; Tue site visit, felt good…

tools.prompt: Audit this week: {week}. Table (Activity | Hours est. | Drain or refill | Why), bullets naming the 3 biggest drains and the 2 most reliable refills, steps to rebalance next week by moving or shrinking specific drains, and a callout on the one thing to protect even on the worst day.

tools.title: Say no gracefully
tools.subtitle: Scripts for a specific ask
tools.prompt: Write a {tone} boundary for the request '{ask}' from my {who}. Quote with the exact words to say or send (under 80 words) followed by a second short version for when they push back, bullets on a trade-off to offer if I genuinely can, and a callout on what not to apologise for.

tools.title: Recovery plan
tools.subtitle: Fourteen days to refill
tools.prompt: Build a 14-day recovery plan given {leave} off and these non-negotiables: {nonneg}. Table (Day | Rest | Movement | Connection | Work limit), a checklist of things to switch off or hand over before it starts, bullets on what recovery actually feels like in week 1 versus week 2, and a callout on the difference between rest and numbing.

tools.title: Talk to my manager
tools.subtitle: Prepare the conversation

inputs.label: Context
inputs.placeholder: 3 people left, I'm covering two roles

tools.prompt: Prepare a conversation with my manager asking for '{goal}', context: {context}. Steps for the conversation (open, evidence, ask, close), a quote with the opening three sentences, a table (Likely objection | Response), and a callout on what to put in writing afterwards.

disclaimer: Not therapy or medical advice. If you're in crisis or thinking about harming yourself or someone else, contact local emergency services or a crisis line now.
